name: Tag
summary: Use a tag to show a concise status or category that helps users scan related information.
whenToUse: Use to label an item's current status in a list, table, task list or banner.
Use a documented colour variant only when a consistent status meaning exists across the service.
whenNotToUse: Do not use tags as buttons, links or interactive filters.
Do not use a tag merely to decorate or emphasise ordinary text.
Do not create many colour meanings that users must memorise.

anatomy.name: Tag element
anatomy.description: A govuk-tag wraps a short status label; choose an element that fits the surrounding semantics.

anatomy.name: Status label
anatomy.description: Brief text communicates the status without relying on the background colour.

variants.name: Default blue
variants.use: A status where no documented semantic colour variant is needed.

variants.name: Green
variants.use: A positive or completed state, used consistently.

variants.name: Red
variants.use: A stopped, rejected or urgent negative state, used consistently.

variants.name: Grey
variants.use: An inactive, closed or neutral state.

behaviour: Tags have no JavaScript behaviour and must not receive interactive roles or click handlers.
Keep status terminology and colour mapping consistent across the product.
accessibility: The label text must communicate the full status independently of colour.
Make repeated tags meaningful in their row or item context.
Do not add tabindex to a non-interactive tag.
content: Use one to three short words and sentence case unless the product's established status vocabulary requires otherwise.
Prefer specific labels such as “Completed” or “Needs review” over vague labels such as “Status 2”.
